caveats: These are the agent's own labels, not an independent human's - the same
caveat as eval/m2/labels.json, and it binds harder here: a 99 % gate on
~235 items means two mistakes spends the whole budget.
Two boxes (f327 #1 and #5) bound a thrower and the defender marking them in
one box. They are labelled unsure and excluded from the team gate, because
no team assignment for them can be right. They are counted and reported
rather than quietly dropped. M2 recorded the same pair as its only class of
miss.
**These labels disagree with eval/m2/labels.json on three frames, and the
disagreement is not resolved in M2's favour.** M2 counted people per frame;
this pass judged every box individually at 2-8x with the box outline drawn
on it. On f194, f210 and f226 M2 counted one, two and one more non-player
respectively than this pass finds. Every f210 box was then re-examined at 7x
(zoom_d.png): all fourteen are players, four of them Chill players wearing
numbers 28, 23, 51 and 4. The far-side figures M2 may have read as crew sit
at soccer y = 11.6 to 16.0, several yards inside the far sideline at +20.58,
at height ratios 0.64 to 0.88. M2's own caveat allows about +/-1 per crowded
frame; this is that, plus one frame at +/-2.
The consequence is that M2's measured false-positive rate of 1.35/frame was
slightly pessimistic. The honest reading of both passes together is that the
true in-bounds non-player count over these 20 frames is 23, not 27. M3's
reject gate is measured against 23 and says so.

team_gate.unsure_note: boxes bounding a Sol and a Chill player together; no team assignment for them can be right

reject_gate.note: M2 deferred its false-positive gate to M3. This is that gate, re-measured with appearance available. The denominator is this pass's per-box count of non-players, not M2's per-frame count; they differ by four and eval/m3/team_labels.json says why.
